title: C++ DSA roadmap
description: A practical path from C++ fundamentals to contest-ready problem solving. Use Striver’s A2Z sheet for exercises alongside these CodeFAMT learning checkpoints. Mark each topic complete at your own pace.

steps.title: C++ foundations
steps.description: Write functions, use references, and understand types, loops and input/output. Practise small arithmetic and string exercises.

steps.title: Time and space complexity
steps.description: Estimate loop costs, compare growth rates and recognise when a solution will exceed the constraints.

steps.title: STL essentials
steps.description: Practise vector, string, pair, set, map, unordered_map, stack, queue and priority_queue. Learn iterators and custom sorting.

steps.title: Basic maths and recursion
steps.description: Implement gcd, prime checks and digit operations. Trace recursive calls and define reliable base cases.

steps.title: Sorting
steps.description: Implement selection, insertion, merge and quick sort. Explain stability and choose an appropriate algorithm.

steps.title: Arrays and prefix sums
steps.description: Work through traversal, rotation, frequency counting and prefix sums. Include empty, negative and duplicate cases.

steps.title: Binary search
steps.description: Search sorted data, find boundaries and apply binary search to a monotonic answer space.

steps.title: Strings and hashing
steps.description: Practise palindrome checks, character frequencies and anagrams. Understand how hashing speeds up lookups.

steps.title: Two pointers and sliding windows
steps.description: Build fixed and variable windows. State the condition that lets a pointer move without missing an answer.

steps.title: Linked lists
steps.description: Reverse a list, find its middle and detect cycles. Draw pointer changes before coding them.

steps.title: Stacks and queues
steps.description: Solve balanced brackets and next-greater-element tasks. Learn monotonic stacks and queue-based processing.

steps.title: Recursion and backtracking
steps.description: Generate subsets and permutations. Track the decision, recursive call and undo step; avoid duplicate answers.

steps.title: Bit manipulation
steps.description: Use masks, shifts and XOR. Practise testing and setting bits and counting set bits.

steps.title: Greedy algorithms and heaps
steps.description: Explain why each greedy choice is safe. Use heaps for top-k values and scheduling.

steps.title: Trees and binary search trees
steps.description: Write DFS and BFS traversals. Practise height, diameter, paths and BST search and validation.

steps.title: Graphs
steps.description: Build adjacency lists. Practise components, cycle detection, topological ordering, shortest paths and disjoint sets.

steps.title: Dynamic programming
steps.description: Define state, transition and base cases. Progress from one-dimensional recurrence to grid, subsequence and knapsack problems.

steps.title: Tries and revision
steps.description: Build a prefix trie, then revisit weak topics. Complete timed mixed sets and review failed approaches before attempting contests.
